back: Finance needed to set up a business: first assets, opening stock, deposits and early expenses.
Start-up, expansion, replacing non-current assets, new technology, working capital, temporary cash shortages.
Spending on non-current assets used for more than a year (buildings, machinery, vehicles).
Spending on day-to-day running costs (wages, rent, electricity, materials).
Short-term: stock, wages, seasonal gaps (under a year). Long-term: buildings, machinery, expansion (many years).
Finance long-term needs with long-term sources and short-term needs with short-term sources.
Long-term (fixed) capital is invested in non-current assets; short-term capital finances current assets and daily operations.
External finance = total finance needed − funds already available (savings, retained profit).
